title: Formatting, documentation and opam packaging
body: `ocamlformat` gives a whole team one layout, so reviews are about behaviour and not about spacing. A `.ocamlformat` file in the project root pins the formatter's version and options, and `dune build @fmt` reports every file that would change; `dune fmt` (or `dune promote`) rewrites them. Pin the version, because different versions format differently.

`odoc` turns documentation comments written as `(** ... *)` into HTML. A library with a `public_name` belongs to a package, and `dune build @doc` builds the pages under `_build/default/_doc/_html`. Document the interface (`.mli`) rather than the implementation, and give each public value one sentence about what it returns.

Opam is the package manager, and Dune can generate the package description from the project. With `(generate_opam_files true)` and a `(package ...)` stanza in `dune-project`, `dune build` writes `tidy.opam` for you, so the dependency list lives in one place. Edit `dune-project`, never the generated `.opam` file.
challenge: The starter builds but `dune build @fmt` reports src/tidy.ml and src/tidy.mli as unformatted. Replace them with the formatted versions (or run `dune fmt`), then confirm the opam file mentions the package synopsis and the docs build.
projectInstructions: Run `dune build @fmt --root .` to see the formatting diff, then `dune fmt --root .` to apply it. Run `dune build --root .` to generate tidy.opam and `dune build @doc --root .` for the documentation.
question: Why pin a version in `.ocamlformat`?
correct: Different ocamlformat versions format differently, so a pin keeps everyone's output identical
wrong: Without a pin, ocamlformat refuses to run on comments
reasoning: A shared formatter only removes style churn if every contributor and CI job runs the same version.
